description: ENTRY POINTS: The execution layer. This defines HOW the resolved packages (index.json) from the declared universe (lock.json) are EXECUTED when the user runs ContentExportFramework.exe

ContentExportFramework.description: Main application entry point - starts CLI menu

entry_point_flow.step_1: User double-clicks ContentExportFramework.exe on Desktop (or Start Menu)
entry_point_flow.step_3: Python runtime is extracted from .exe to temp directory
entry_point_flow.step_4: All locked packages extracted to temp (python-docx, openpyxl, requests, etc.)
entry_point_flow.step_5: All internal modules extracted to temp (copilot_*.py, word_search_engine.py, etc.)
entry_point_flow.step_8: CLI menu is displayed to user
entry_point_flow.step_10: Selected process executes using extracted modules and dependencies
entry_point_flow.step_12: User can optionally sync to OneDrive
entry_point_flow.step_13: Program exits or loops to menu
entry_point_flow.step_14: Temp files cleaned up by Windows temp cleaner (later)

interactive.behavior: Display menu, wait for user input
interactive.description: The ONLY execution mode in v1.0

command_line_args.reason: Out of scope for v1.0 (future enhancement)

1.name: Start Copilot Export Pipeline
1.interactive_steps: Prompts for browser auth in step 2

4.name: Restore from OneDrive
4.warning: Overwrites local with newer OneDrive versions

error_handling.file_not_found: Display error message, prompt user retry
error_handling.oauth_timeout: Display timeout message, instruct manual browser auth

interlock_with_lock_and_index.relationship: All three are orthogonal but interlock. Lock defines boundary. Index resolves it. Entry Points execute it.

execution_guarantee: When user clicks ContentExportFramework.exe, everything needed is inside. No external registry. No external index server. No plugins. No distributed components. Just one file, complete in itself.
